story.title: Putin Observes Naval Drills Before Controversial Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands
story.summary: President Vladimir Putin observed naval exercises off Sakhalin Island before making a controversial visit to the Kuril Islands, which Japan claims. This visit has prompted strong protests from Japan, with officials labeling it 'unacceptable' and summoning the Russian ambassador to express their discontent. This marks the first visit by a Russian leader to the disputed islands since they were seized by the Soviet Union in 1945.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed with Putin’s visit?
explore_lenses.title: A presidential visit raised the stakes
explore_lenses.summary: Putin’s August 13, 2026 stop on Iturup was his first visit to the disputed islands as president, following Pacific Fleet drills near Sakhalin. It was not the first visit by any Russian leader: then-President Dmitry Medvedev visited in 2010.

claims.text: Putin visited Iturup, met Sakhalin regional governor Valery Limarenko, and toured a fish plant, hospital, and school after attending Pacific Fleet exercises near Sakhalin.
The supplied characterization that this was the first Russian leader’s visit is inaccurate: reporting identifies it as Putin’s first visit, while Dmitry Medvedev visited the Kurils in 2010.

Putin said the islands’ current status was established by the outcome of World War II and reflected in international documents, while saying Russia had been prepared to seek a peace-treaty solution with Japan.

explore_lenses.label: What do Tokyo and Moscow say they own?
explore_lenses.title: The sovereignty claims directly conflict
explore_lenses.summary: Japan claims four southern islands as its Northern Territories; Russia administers them as part of the Kurils. Each government grounds its position in a different reading of the post-World War II settlement.

claims.text: Japan’s Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi said Japan strongly protested the visit and described the Northern Territories, including Etorofu/Iturup, as inherently Japanese territory historically and under international law.
Russia controls the island chain; Japan’s claim covers the four southernmost islands—Iturup/Etorofu, Kunashir/Kunashiri, Shikotan, and Habomai—taken by the Soviet Union at the end of World War II.

Japan’s 2025 Diplomatic Bluebook calls the islands Japanese territory under Russian occupation; Russia’s position, as expressed by Putin, is that their present status follows the results of World War II.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next diplomatically?
explore_lenses.title: The dispute remains in a frozen channel
explore_lenses.summary: Japan has formally protested by summoning Russia’s ambassador, but the underlying peace-treaty process has been stalled since 2022. The immediate step is diplomatic messaging, not a process that automatically changes control of the islands.

claims.text: Motegi summoned Russian Ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev, lodged a strong protest over Putin’s visit, and asked that the message be promptly reported to Moscow.
The territorial dispute has prevented Japan and Russia from signing a formal peace treaty ending their World War II hostilities.

Japan’s Foreign Ministry says Russia discontinued peace-treaty talks in March 2022, suspended related exchange programs, and withdrew from talks on joint economic activity; Japan says it will continue pursuing a treaty through resolution of the islands’ status.
Forecast: Japan’s stated policy is to keep seeking a peace treaty tied to resolving the four-island question, but the ministry’s account indicates no active negotiating channel has been restored.

story_report.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin observed Pacific Fleet naval exercises off Sakhalin Island before visiting Iturup, one of the Russian-controlled Kuril Islands claimed by Japan. Japan called the visit “unacceptable,” with Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi lodging a strong protest and summoning Russia’s ambassador. The trip was Putin’s first visit to the islands, not the first by a Russian leader: former President Dmitry Medvedev visited in 2010. The dispute remains a central obstacle to a formal Japan-Russia peace treaty ending World War II hostilities.

sections.heading: Japan and Russia contest sovereignty
sections.body: Russia controls the Kuril island chain, while Japan claims its four southernmost islands: Iturup, known in Japan as Etorofu; Kunashir; Shikotan; and Habomai. Japan says the Northern Territories are inherently Japanese territory historically and under international law, and its 2025 Diplomatic Bluebook describes them as under Russian occupation. Putin said their current status was established by the outcome of World War II and reflected in international documents.

sections.heading: Putin visit deepens stalled diplomacy
sections.body: During his trip, Putin met Sakhalin regional governor Valery Limarenko and toured a fish plant, hospital and school on Iturup. Japan says Russia discontinued peace-treaty talks in March 2022, suspended related exchange programs and withdrew from discussions on joint economic activity. Tokyo says it will continue seeking a peace treaty through resolution of the islands’ status, but the reviewed material indicates no active negotiating channel has been restored.

related_stories.title: Karoline Leavitt to Depart as White House Press Secretary
related_stories.summary: Karoline Leavitt will step down from her role as White House press secretary at the end of the month, as announced by President Donald Trump. Leavitt described her decision as bittersweet, having recently returned to work after the birth of her second child. She is noted for being the youngest person to hold the position and will continue as a senior advisor following her departure.
